title: Integral Chow modification with a relatively ample projective-space line bundle
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme], separated and of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There exist an integer $N\geq0$, an integral separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$, a proper surjective $k$-morphism $\pi:Y\to X$ [def-weil-surjective-morphism], an immersion $j:Y\to\mathbf P^N_k$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], and a nonempty open $U\subseteq X$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism. The invertible module $\mathcal L=j^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^N_k}(1)$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-projective-space-twist, def-sc-invertible-module] is $\pi$-relatively ample: for every affine open $W\subseteq X$, $\mathcal L|_{\pi^{-1}(W)}$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. No properness hypothesis on $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is made.

source.place: Tag 0201, label remark-chow-Noetherian (2),(3), following lemma-chow-Noetherian; relative ampleness by morphisms.tex Tag 02NR, label lemma-characterize-ample-on-finite-type; the precise use is etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0A3M, Chow paragraph

proof.text: Apply ChowModification over Spec k, which is Noetherian, to obtain Z, proper surjective p, an immersion j₀ into projective space with finite coordinate type, and a dense open U over which p is an isomorphism. U is nonempty since X is integral. Put V = p⁻¹(U). The isomorphism V → U shows V is nonempty and integral. Finite type over k makes Z locally Noetherian, so the inclusion of V is quasi-compact; no affine shrinking of U is needed.

source.place: Tag 0201, label remark-chow-Noetherian (2),(3), following lemma-chow-Noetherian; relative ampleness by morphisms.tex Tag 02NR, label lemma-characterize-ample-on-finite-type; the precise use is etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0A3M, Chow paragraph

proof.text: Take Y = image(V → Z) with closed immersion c and factor v:V → Y. The quasi-compact factor v is scheme-theoretically dominant, hence its section maps are injective. Because V is reduced, injectivity makes all section rings of Y reduced (Mathlib IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant.isReduced). The image of the irreducible V under v is irreducible; its closure is all of Y by dominance. Thus Y is irreducible and reduced, hence integral. The schematic closure inclusion c restricts to an isomorphism over V, by Scheme.Opens.isIso_morphismRestrict_imageι.

source.place: Tag 0201, label remark-chow-Noetherian (2),(3), following lemma-chow-Noetherian; relative ampleness by morphisms.tex Tag 02NR, label lemma-characterize-ample-on-finite-type; the precise use is etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0A3M, Chow paragraph

proof.text: Set π = c ≫ p. It is proper as a composite of proper morphisms. The composite v ≫ π equals the isomorphism V → U followed by U → X; this is dominant since U is dense. Dominance descends to π, and proper dominant morphisms are surjective. The restriction of π over U is the composite of the two known isomorphisms. Composition gives separatedness and finite type of Y over k. Compose c with j₀ to obtain an immersion over k. The coordinate type is nonempty: a point of V maps to projective space, whose standard opens cover. Apply exists_reindexed_projective_immersion to replace its finite coordinate type by ULift (Fin (N+1)), preserving the immersion and its structure-map identity.

source.place: Tag 0201, label remark-chow-Noetherian (2),(3), following lemma-chow-Noetherian; relative ampleness by morphisms.tex Tag 02NR, label lemma-characterize-ample-on-finite-type; the precise use is etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0A3M, Chow paragraph

proof.text: Let a = ProjectiveSpace.liftBaseChange π j. Its composite with the map to projective space over k is j, so a is an immersion by cancellation. Its composite with the proper, hence separated, projection to X is π, so a is proper by IsProper.of_comp. A proper immersion is a closed immersion. This does not require X to be proper over k.

proof.text: The current ProjectiveSpace.twist is by definition the usual pullback of the integral-model Proj twist. The tensor pullback is left adjoint to pushforward, so uniqueness of left adjoints identifies it with the usual pullback; this identifies the statement’s line bundle with j-star rho_k-star Proj.twist(1) and proves its invertibility. Composite tensor pullback and liftBaseChange_toProjInt identify this module with a-star rho_X-star Proj.twist(1). No comparison with a separately glued model is required. The existing private theorem tensorPullback_invertible from Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.ChowRelativeAmpleTwistProperties supplies preservation of invertibility, and its tensorPullback_pair_iso supplies the composite comparison; both are accessed through a proof-only import all, with no duplicate helper declarations.

source.place: Tag 0201, label remark-chow-Noetherian (2),(3), following lemma-chow-Noetherian; relative ampleness by morphisms.tex Tag 02NR, label lemma-characterize-ample-on-finite-type; the precise use is etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0A3M, Chow paragraph

proof.text: Use the existing private theorem projective_ample_affine_open in Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.ChowRelativeAmpleTwistProperties, accessed through a proof-only import all. It applies to a closed immersion over any base scheme, requiring no properness of that base over a field: its proof identifies each affine open with its section spectrum, applies projective_closedImmersion_ample_invertible, and transports the result along composite pullback isomorphisms. Apply it to a:Y → P^N_X and π:Y → X, obtaining ampleness on each π⁻¹(W). The existing tensorPullback_pair_iso compares j-star rho_k-star Proj.twist(1) with a-star rho_X-star Proj.twist(1) using liftBaseChange_toProjInt. Restrict this isomorphism, compose it with the tensor-versus-usual-pullback comparison from the preceding step, and transfer invertibility and ampleness by isAmple_iff_of_iso. This also covers the empty affine open. No affine-base or pullback helper is restated in this module.
